title: Angular-spectrum optics and controlled paraxial limits

items.title: Uniform phase-multiplier bound for the square-root dispersion law
items.design_state: local mathematical prerequisite proved on the A page; independent review pending
items.statement:
Let $k_0>0$, $0<\delta<1$, $z\in\mathbb R$, and $s\in[0,\delta^2]$. Define

$$R(s):=1-\frac{s}{2}-\sqrt{1-s}.$$

Then

$$R(s)=\frac{s^2}{4\left(1-\frac{s}{2}+\sqrt{1-s}\right)},\qquad 0\le R(s)\le\frac{s^2}{8(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}},$$

and

$$\left|e^{izk_0\sqrt{1-s}}-e^{izk_0(1-s/2)}\right| \le \frac{|z|k_0s^2}{8(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}}.$$

More generally, for all real $a,b$,
$$|e^{ia}-e^{ib}|\le|a-b|.$$

references.title: Konijnenberg, Adam and Urbach, BSc Optics, §6.3 Angular Spectrum Method
references.locator: §6.3, angular-spectrum propagation and the positive square-root longitudinal wave number; the present uniform remainder estimate is proved locally.

references.title: Alexander Cerjan and Charles Cerjan, Orbital angular momentum of Laguerre–Gaussian beams beyond the paraxial approximation, JOSA A 28 (2011)
references.locator: §2, equations (2), (8), and (11), PDF pp. 2253–2254: angular-spectrum data and the square-root dispersion factor; the uniform inequality here is proved locally.

items.title: Forward angular-spectrum beam
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; authored for batch 10; independent review pending
items.statement:
Fix a named positively oriented inertial laboratory chart with coordinates
$(x,y,z,t)$, spatial domain $\mathbb R^3$, and time domain $\mathbb R$. Adopt SI
units, a vacuum speed $c>0$, an angular frequency $\omega>0$, and
$k_0:=\omega/c$ (so $[k_0]=\mathrm{m}^{-1}$). Let
$\mathbf x_\perp:=(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2$. Use the unitary two-dimensional
Fourier transform $\mathcal F_2$ whose Schwartz-space convention is
$$\widehat f(\boldsymbol\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}f(\mathbf x_\perp) e^{-2\pi i\mathbf x_\perp\cdot\boldsymbol\xi}\,d^2\mathbf x_\perp,$$
and whose inverse is its unitary $L^2$ extension. The variable
$\boldsymbol\xi$ is in cycles per metre; its associated angular spatial
wavevector is $\mathbf q:=2\pi\boldsymbol\xi$ in $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$, with
$|\mathbf q|^2:=q_x^2+q_y^2$.

Choose $0<\delta<1$ and $u_0\in L^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)$ with
$\mathcal F_2u_0$ supported, up to null sets, in
$D_\delta:=\{\boldsymbol\xi:|2\pi\boldsymbol\xi|\le\delta k_0\}$.
For $z\in\mathbb R$ put
$$k_z(\boldsymbol\xi):=\sqrt{k_0^2-|2\pi\boldsymbol\xi|^2},$$
which is real and strictly positive on $D_\delta$, and define the exact scalar
and paraxial scalar propagators as the $L^2$ equivalence classes
$$u_{\mathrm{exact}}(z):=\mathcal F_2^{-1}\!\left[ e^{izk_z(\boldsymbol\xi)}\,\mathcal F_2u_0(\boldsymbol\xi)\right],\qquad u_{\mathrm{par}}(z):=e^{ik_0z}\mathcal F_2^{-1}\!\left[ e^{-iz|2\pi\boldsymbol\xi|^2/(2k_0)}\,\mathcal F_2u_0(\boldsymbol\xi)\right].$$
The associated real scalar fields are the real parts of these phasors multiplied
by $e^{-i\omega t}$. If $u_0$ carries $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$, both propagated
fields carry the same unit. “Exact” here names the exact positive axial
dispersion multiplier inside this scalar model; it does not assert exact
Maxwell validity. Forward propagation is $z\ge0$; the formulas also define the
mathematical continuation to negative $z$.

At a fixed $\boldsymbol\xi\in D_\delta$, write
$\mathbf K(\boldsymbol\xi):=(2\pi\xi_x,2\pi\xi_y,k_z(\boldsymbol\xi))$.
A candidate monochromatic vector plane-wave mode at frequency $\omega$ has
complex amplitudes $\mathbf e,\mathbf b\in\mathbb C^3$ in the real-field
encoding $e^{i(\mathbf K\cdot(x,y,z)-\omega t)}$. It is called an exact
source-free vacuum mode only when its associated real fields satisfy the
adopted source-free vacuum Maxwell equations. The longitudinal electric
coefficient is $e_z$, and
$\mathbf e_\perp:=(e_x,e_y)$ has norm
$|\mathbf e_\perp|^2:=|e_x|^2+|e_y|^2$. No scalar/vector polarization
factorization is part of this definition.
items.physical_scope: Idealized classical scalar optics in a fixed inertial laboratory chart and SI units, for square-integrable plane data whose two-dimensional spatial-frequency support lies in a forward propagating cone strictly inside the vacuum light cone. The compact-aperture postulate supplies scalar-optics context but does not imply that every compact-aperture output belongs to this band-limited finite-energy class. The scalar propagation operators are not asserted to be exact Maxwell fields; exact vector plane-wave modes are treated separately. No empirical claim, measurement, or quantization is made.

references.title: Konijnenberg, Adam and Urbach, BSc Optics, §6.3 Angular Spectrum Method
references.locator: Complete §6.3: two-dimensional Fourier decomposition, positive square-root longitudinal wave number for forward propagation with $e^{-i\omega t}$, and the propagating/evanescent split.

references.title: Niklas Beisert, Elektrodynamik, ETH Zürich 2024 FS lecture notes
references.locator: §11.1 'Fourier-Raum', equations (11.5)–(11.10), PDF pp. 121–122: source-free Maxwell Fourier modes, dispersion, transversality, and the electric/magnetic amplitude relation.

references.title: Alexander Cerjan and Charles Cerjan, Orbital angular momentum of Laguerre–Gaussian beams beyond the paraxial approximation, JOSA A 28 (2011)
references.locator: §2, equations (2), (8), PDF pp. 2253–2254: angular-spectrum data and the positive propagation branch; no arbitrary compact-aperture data are inferred.

items.title: Paraxial phase and longitudinal-field bounds
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; authored for batch 10; independent review pending
items.statement:
Let $k_0>0$, $0<\delta<1$, and $z\in\mathbb R$. For every
$u_0\in L^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)$ whose Fourier transform is supported, up
to null sets, in
$D_\delta:=\{\boldsymbol\xi:|2\pi\boldsymbol\xi|\le\delta k_0\}$,

$$\left\|u_{\mathrm{exact}}(z)-u_{\mathrm{par}}(z)\right\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^2)} \le \frac{|z|k_0\delta^4}{8(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}}\left\|u_0\right\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^2)},$$

where the propagated fields are exactly those of the angular-spectrum
Definition. For a source-free monochromatic vacuum plane-wave mode with
$\mathbf q:=2\pi\boldsymbol\xi$, $|\mathbf q|\le\delta k_0$,
$k_z:=\sqrt{k_0^2-|\mathbf q|^2}$, and complex electric amplitude
$\mathbf e=(\mathbf e_\perp,e_z)$, use the complex-bilinear convention
$\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf e_\perp:=q_xe_x+q_ye_y$ with no conjugation,

$$e_z=-\frac{\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf e_\perp}{k_z},\qquad |e_z|\le\frac{\delta}{\sqrt{1-\delta^2}}|\mathbf e_\perp|.$$
items.physical_scope: Conditional result for the ideal band-limited scalar angular-spectrum model and smooth source-free monochromatic vacuum plane-wave modes in the same fixed inertial chart and SI convention. It bounds the scalar Helmholtz phase approximation and the longitudinal electric amplitude only; it does not say that finite-aperture data have the required band limit, that the scalar model is exact Maxwell theory, or that a finite sample or measurement obeys the bound. No empirical conclusion or angular-momentum decomposition is asserted.

references.title: Konijnenberg, Adam and Urbach, BSc Optics, §6.3 Angular Spectrum Method
references.locator: Complete §6.3, especially the propagating-wave multiplier and the final vector-transversality remark; the uniform $L^2$ error bound is proved locally.

references.title: Niklas Beisert, Elektrodynamik, ETH Zürich 2024 FS lecture notes
references.locator: §11.1 'Fourier-Raum', equations (11.5)–(11.10), PDF pp. 121–122: source-free Maxwell mode constraints and amplitude relations.

references.title: Alexander Cerjan and Charles Cerjan, Orbital angular momentum of Laguerre–Gaussian beams beyond the paraxial approximation, JOSA A 28 (2011)
references.locator: §2 equation (8), §4 equations (22), (29), and (37), PDF pp. 2254–2257: exact angular-spectrum phase and longitudinal vector-field components; this item proves a separate uniform cone estimate.

items.title: Paraxial orbital winding in its exact scalar domain
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; authored for batch 10; independent review pending
items.statement:
Fix a propagation plane $z$ and let $u_z\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)
\cap L^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)$ be a scalar field in the paraxial model.
Assume $u_z$ is nonzero as an $L^2$ equivalence class. For $r>0$ write
$u_z(r\cos\phi,r\sin\phi)=f(r)e^{i\ell\phi}$, where
$\ell\in\mathbb Z$ and $\phi$ is read modulo $2\pi$. Require a smooth
axis extension; explicitly, assume there are $\epsilon>0$ and a smooth
complex-valued $g:(-\epsilon,\epsilon)\to\mathbb C$ such that
$f(r)=r^{|\ell|}g(r^2)$ for $0<r<\sqrt\epsilon$. Define
$L_z^{\mathrm{sc}}:=-i(-y\partial_x+x\partial_y)$ and use the
first-variable-linear $L^2$ pairing
$$\langle v,w\rangle_2:=\int_{\mathbb R^2}v(x,y)\overline{w(x,y)}\,d^2x.$$
Then the normalized scalar angular-generator expectation is
$$\frac{\langle L_z^{\mathrm{sc}}u_z,u_z\rangle_2} {\langle u_z,u_z\rangle_2}=\ell.$$
items.physical_scope: Conditional identity for a smooth, finite-transverse-norm scalar paraxial field in the specified angular-spectrum model, at a fixed propagation plane. The dimensionless scalar rotation generator is not identified with torque, total electromagnetic angular momentum, a photon angular momentum, or a general exact-vector spin/orbital decomposition. No empirical claim is made.

references.title: Alexander Cerjan and Charles Cerjan, Orbital angular momentum of Laguerre–Gaussian beams beyond the paraxial approximation, JOSA A 28 (2011)
references.locator: §1 and §5, PDF pp. 2253 and 2257–2258: the paraxial scalar winding parameter and the scope limits of its relation to full vector angular-momentum flux.

title: Angular-spectrum optics and controlled paraxial limits — Examples

items.title: A small angular cone can accumulate order-one phase error
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; authored for batch 10; independent review pending
items.statement:
For every sequence $(\delta_n)_{n\ge1}$ with $\delta_n\in(0,1)$ and
$\delta_n\to0$, every fixed $k_0>0$, every nonzero scalar input
$u_{0,n}\in L^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)$
whose Fourier support lies in $|2\pi\boldsymbol\xi|\le\delta_n k_0$, and every
sequence of forward distances $z_n>0$ satisfying
$z_nk_0\delta_n^4=8\pi$, the relative exact-to-paraxial error tends to zero:

$$\frac{\|u_{\mathrm{exact},n}(z_n)-u_{\mathrm{par},n}(z_n)\|_2} {\|u_{0,n}\|_2}\longrightarrow0.$$
items.physical_scope: Counterexample inside the ideal band-limited scalar angular-spectrum model in a fixed inertial chart and SI units. Its spectra are square-integrable plane data and are not asserted to be outputs of a compact finite aperture. It is a conditional model calculation, not an observed optical result.

references.title: Konijnenberg, Adam and Urbach, BSc Optics, §6.3 Angular Spectrum Method
references.locator: §6.3: exact square-root propagating multiplier; this counterexample constructs its own supported $L^2$ spectra.

references.title: Alexander Cerjan and Charles Cerjan, Orbital angular momentum of Laguerre–Gaussian beams beyond the paraxial approximation, JOSA A 28 (2011)
references.locator: §2 equation (8) and discussion of the positive propagation root and excluded evanescent components, PDF p. 2254; the annular sequence and phase limit here are proved locally.

references.title: Niklas Beisert, Elektrodynamik, ETH Zürich 2024 FS lecture notes
references.locator: §11.1 Fourier-space solution, equations (11.5)–(11.10), PDF pp. 121–122; no vector angular-momentum claim is made in this scalar counterexample.

items.title: Tight focusing changes polarization bookkeeping
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; authored for batch 10; independent review pending
items.statement:
Let $0<\kappa\le\delta k_0$, $\mathbf q=(\kappa,0)$,
$k_z:=\sqrt{k_0^2-\kappa^2}$, and choose a real $E_0\ne0$ in
$\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$. Put
$$\mathbf e:=(E_0,0,-\kappa E_0/k_z),\qquad \mathbf b:=\left(0,\frac{k_0^2E_0}{\omega k_z},0\right),\qquad \phi(\mathbf x,t):=\kappa x+k_z z-\omega t.$$
The real fields $E(\mathbf x,t):=\operatorname{Re}(\mathbf e e^{i\phi(\mathbf x,t)})$
and $B(\mathbf x,t):=\operatorname{Re}(\mathbf b e^{i\phi(\mathbf x,t)})$ are an exact, forward,
source-free vacuum plane-wave mode. In particular,
$$e_z=-\frac{\kappa E_0}{\sqrt{k_0^2-\kappa^2}}\ne0,\qquad \frac{|e_z|}{|E_0|}=\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt{k_0^2-\kappa^2}} \le\frac{\delta}{\sqrt{1-\delta^2}}.$$
Thus setting $e_z=0$ while keeping this transverse amplitude would not give an
exact Maxwell mode.
items.physical_scope: Exact plane-wave example in the smooth, source-free vacuum Maxwell model and the propagating cone of the ideal angular-spectrum model. It illustrates the longitudinal component required by Maxwell's equations; it asserts no measured field, focal apparatus, or torque.

references.title: Konijnenberg, Adam and Urbach, BSc Optics, §6.3 Angular Spectrum Method
references.locator: §6.3 final vector-field remark: longitudinal electric components are fixed by the momentum-space transversality condition.

references.title: Alexander Cerjan and Charles Cerjan, Orbital angular momentum of Laguerre–Gaussian beams beyond the paraxial approximation, JOSA A 28 (2011)
references.locator: §4 equations (22), (29), and (37), PDF pp. 2256–2257: longitudinal electric field is reconstructed from transverse data under Maxwell transversality.

references.title: Niklas Beisert, Elektrodynamik, ETH Zürich 2024 FS lecture notes
references.locator: §11.1 Fourier-Raum, equations (11.5)–(11.10), PDF pp. 121–122: the exact vector amplitude satisfies $\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf e=0$.
